summary: Added UI.card(title, body, opts) to components.js with full opts support: id, dataId, style, accentColor, titleStyle, extraClass
Replaced all 8 inline card constructions in work-package.js with UI.card() calls
Replaced 2 card constructions in knowledge.js using opts.dataId to preserve event delegation
Replaced 1 card construction in config.js using opts.style for max-width constraint
Replaced 1 card construction in project-detail.js
Refactored renderStatusCard() in orchestrator-widgets.js to use UI.card() with extraClass and status-driven accentColor
Added accentColor field to statusMeta() return objects mapping status to CSS colour variables
Added box-shadow: none to .orchestrator-status-card CSS to suppress card base shadow and preserve visual appearance
Verified in browser: no JS errors, correct HTML structure, config max-width respected, dark/light theme compatible

comments.note: components.js: The UI.card() opts API is intentionally broader than the AC-specified minimum (opts.accentColor + title/body). The additional opts (id, dataId, style, titleStyle, extraClass) were required to cover all 13 migration call sites without compromise. The API remains cohesive and self-documenting.

orchestrator-widgets.js renderStatusCard(): The old imperative string-building pattern (html += ...) has been replaced with a declarative single-return UI.card() call. The accentColor mapping in statusMeta() is a clean extension that required no structural changes to the function.

styles.css: The .orchestrator-status-card block now partially duplicates .card properties (background, border, border-radius). Now that it extends .card via the extraClass mechanism, a future cleanup could remove the redundant shared properties from .orchestrator-status-card, leaving only the overrides (padding, margin-bottom, box-shadow: none). Out of scope for this WP.

work-package.js: The WP spec counted 7 card fragments; the actual file contained 8 (the error-fallback catch block for dialogues at the bottom). All 8 were migrated. The spec count was slightly off but all cases were handled correctly.

summary: AC1-3 (UI.card API): Verified in live browser — all three call signatures produce correct HTML output (title present/absent, accentColor sets border-left-color inline style).
AC4 (work-package.js): All 8 card fragments use UI.card() — spec counted 7, actual was 8 (error-fallback catch block). All migrated correctly.
AC5 (all view files): UI.card() calls confirmed in knowledge.js (×2), config.js, project-detail.js, orchestrator-widgets.js.
AC6 (orchestrator-status-card): renderStatusCard() uses UI.card() with extraClass and status-driven accentColor. statusMeta() returns correct CSS variable per status.
AC7 (visual appearance): Config card verified in both dark and light themes — correct border, background, border-radius, max-width constraint, padding.
AC8 (no JS errors): Console error monitoring over Projects, Orchestrator, Config, and Insights pages showed 0 errors.

Regression fix: 14 test failures found and resolved. client-rendering.test.ts and insights-knowledge-links.test.ts were missing components.js in their beforeAll setup. Added componentsJs load before view scripts in both files. All 3095 tests now pass.

comments.note: client-rendering.test.ts did not load components.js before work-package.js/project-detail.js in beforeAll. Both now call UI.card(), causing ReferenceError: UI is not defined at runtime. 8 tests failed. Fixed by adding vm.runInThisContext(componentsJs) after utils.js.

insights-knowledge-links.test.ts did not load components.js before insights.js/knowledge.js in beforeAll. Both now depend on UI namespace (UI.emptyState, UI.filterBar, UI.card). 6 tests failed with incorrect assertion results due to swallowed Promise rejections. Fixed by adding vm.runInThisContext(componentsJs) after utils.js.

AC3 spec says style="border-left-color: #ff0000" (no trailing semicolon). The implementation produces style="border-left-color: #ff0000;" (with trailing semicolon). Both are valid CSS; browsers normalise them identically. No functional impact.

AC4 spec counted 7 card fragments in work-package.js; actual file had 8 (error-fallback catch block for dialogues). Developer correctly migrated all 8. Spec count was slightly off but all cases handled correctly — no action needed.

summary: Reviewed UI.card(title, body, opts) implementation in components.js — clean, well-structured, follows existing IIFE-namespace pattern. Escaping is correctly applied to structural attributes (id, dataId, title) while style-related opts are correctly left unescaped (CSS values, not HTML).

Reviewed all 13 migration call sites across work-package.js (×8), knowledge.js (×2), config.js (×1), project-detail.js (×1), orchestrator-widgets.js (×1) — all correct. Each call site uses exactly the opts needed for its context; no over-/under-engineering.

statusMeta() extension in orchestrator-widgets.js: accentColor field using CSS variable references (var(--color-complete), etc.) is a clean, theme-aware approach. renderStatusCard() reads naturally as a declarative single-return.
QA test fixes (client-rendering.test.ts, insights-knowledge-links.test.ts) are correct and minimal — componentsJs loaded in the right position after utilsJs and before view scripts.

Fix-Forward applied: added JSDoc safety note to UI.card() opts documenting that opts.style, opts.accentColor, and opts.titleStyle are NOT HTML-escaped, consistent with the existing _normaliseType() caveat pattern in the same file.

Two Documentation-Forward items flagged for Documentation agent: (1) api-surface.md components.js section still only documents WP-001 functions — needs UI.card() added; (2) api-surface.md renderStatusCard() entry does not mention the new status-driven accentColor border-left-color output.
Developer debt note on .orchestrator-status-card CSS duplication confirmed accurate and correctly scoped as out-of-WP-006 cleanup.
All 8 acceptance criteria confirmed met by QA pipeline with 3095/3095 tests passing.

Consistent with the existing _normaliseType() safety note in the same file. Non-behavioral — no runtime change.

2. Added full UI.card(title, body, opts?) detail entry in the components.js section: signature, opts breakdown (id, dataId, style, accentColor, titleStyle, extraClass), escaping behaviour (title/id/dataId escaped; style fields verbatim), security note on unescaped opts, and three examples.

3. Updated renderStatusCard() entry in orchestrator-widgets.js section to note the card now uses UI.card() with extraClass and accentColor, and documents the three status-to-colour mappings (green/red/amber via CSS variables).

notes: UI.card() is in components.js and exported on the UI namespace. All 13 call sites across 5 files have been migrated.
The orchestrator-status-card elements now carry class="card orchestrator-status-card" and a status-driven border-left-color inline style (green=started, red=dead, amber=pending).

knowledge.js cards carry data-id via opts.dataId — event delegation in the knowledge view depends on this attribute being present on the card wrapper.

All 8 ACs verified: UI.card() API correct (browser-tested), all 13 call sites migrated, .orchestrator-status-card uses status-driven accentColor, zero JS console errors across all views, visual appearance correct in both themes.
